title: Leaky Borders on the Tree of Life: The Biological Species Concept, Porous Genomes, and the Genomic-Island Illusion — How one gene pool splits in two when hybrids keep mating; Ernst Mayr's allopatric Biological Species Concept & Coyne & Orr's 119-pair Drosophila isolation clock; Chung-I Wu's porous-genome revolution; Feder, Chilcote & Bush's sympatric Rhagoletis apple-maggot shift, Edelman's 20-genome Heliconius butterfly introgression web & Lamichhaney and the Grants' 3-generation Big Bird hybrid finch; Kevin De Queiroz's Unified Lineage Concept & Cruickshank & Hahn's proof that linked selection creates false F_ST speciation islands with low d_XY; migration-recombination & coalescent island math plus spotting speciation models in disguise

teenKit.tldr: Species aren't hermetically sealed biological vaults; modern whole-genome sequencing reveals they are actually porous gene pools that constantly trade DNA even as they split apart.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how porous our genetic boundaries really are reshapes how we understand biodiversity, conservation, and even our own human history with Neanderthals.
keyTakeaways: Ernst Mayr's classic Biological Species Concept defined species as reproductively isolated groups, but whole-genome data shows rampant cross-species gene flow.
Speciation can happen quickly and without geographic barriers, as seen in apple maggot flies switching host plants and Darwin's finches forming new hybrid lineages in just three generations.
Apparent 'genomic islands of speciation' with high F_ST values can actually be statistical illusions caused by linked selection clearing out variation, rather than hard barriers to gene flow.

vocab.meaning: Ernst Mayr's classic idea that a species is a group of actually or potentially interbreeding populations that are reproductively isolated from other groups.
The movement of a gene from one species into the gene pool of another by repeated backcrossing of an interspecific hybrid with one of its parent species.
The evolution of a new species from a surviving ancestral species while both continue to inhabit the same geographic region.
A statistical measure of genetic population differentiation based on allele frequency variance between groups.

quiz.question: What did Chung-I Wu's 'genic view' propose about diverging genomes during speciation?
options: Genomes act as solid, impenetrable vaults separating species completely.
Genomes function as selectively semi-permeable sieves where some genes flow while others are blocked.
Genomes stop mutating entirely once two species begin to separate.
Genomes merge back into a single uniform pool within a single generation.
quiz.explanation: Wu showed that genomes are semi-permeable sieves allowing certain genes to pass between populations while selection blocks others.

quiz.question: How fast did the 'Big Bird' hybrid finch lineage arise on Daphne Major according to the Grants and Lamichhaney?
quiz.explanation: The Grants and Lamichhaney documented the rapid emergence of a reproductively isolated hybrid finch lineage in just three generations.

quiz.question: What did Cruickshank and Hahn discover about celebrated relative F_ST 'genomic islands of speciation'?
options: They had very high absolute divergence (d_XY) values.
They were actually an artifact of linked background selection in allopatry with low d_XY.
They proved Ernst Mayr was entirely correct about physical isolation.
They only existed in laboratory fruit flies.
quiz.explanation: Cruickshank and Hahn proved that high F_ST genomic islands often had low absolute divergence, pointing to background selection rather than barriers to gene flow.
